One traveler comes to this place to fetch some magic tools to repair his broken sled, after taking an earlier trip here to obtain three magic words to build a boat. An old woman comes here equipped with a giant copper rake with which she retrieves pieces of her son, who was killed by a serpent summoned by Nasshut. The old woman uses the copper rake to dredge this place's black river, which is guarded by a sister of Loviatar, and which houses an animal pursued by a hero sent here by Louhi, the queen of Pohjola. Lemminkainen seeks a black swan in what Finnish underworld?

In one part of this work, a character has a vision of a legendary hero while sleeping on a yellow ox skin in a bed full of fleas of. Another part of this work tells of a plague in the form of a scream that causes all of the women in the land to miscarry. Characters in this work include a king who spends all his down time with his feet in the lap of a virgin, and a woman who became stuck to a golden stool while traveling with her son, her daughter-in- law Cigfa, and her second husband Manawydan. Another character is accused of cannibalism after dog blood is smeared on her face. Math ap Mathonwy, Pryderi and Rhiannon all appear in what collection of Welsh stories and myths?

One figure in this work cuts his hair and gnaws off his fingernails, which he gives to ants to fool some opponents into thinking he has died at the bottom of a pit. Two men in this work receive an invitation from a louse swallowed by a toad hidden inside a snake that itself was swallowed by a hawk. Earlier in this work, an elderly couple pose as dentists and defeat a demon by replacing his jeweled teeth with kernels of corn. The priest Francisco Ximenez translated a manuscript of this work, which contains the stories of Vucub- Caquix's downfall and the defeat of the Lords of Xibalba in a ball game by Hunahpu and Xbalanque, the Hero Twins. Name this Mayan religious text.

After this man walked with dogs on Mount Helicon, his mother Chariclo gave him a staff of cornel wood. This man informed Amphityron that Zeus had raped Alcmena. Following his death at Tilphussa, an Argive army sent spoils to this man's daughter Manto. After this man saw two snakes copulating he underwent a sex change, allowing him to give Zeus and Hera his informed verdict that the sexual pleasure of women is ten times that of men. Identify this blind seer who was sought by Odysseus in the underworld, and who revealed Oedipus's crimes.

Herodotus claimed that the Neuri could change into these creatures, and the first modern Serbian dictionary describes these creatures as men that come back to life in order to fornicate with their widows. In medieval times, the Benediction of St. Hubert was thought to be efficacious against these creatures. Native American lore speaks of similar figures known as Skin- Walkers. One of these creatures that lived during the reign of Louis XV was known as the Beast of Gevaudan, and was killed with a special bullet. Name these creatures that transform during the full moon.

This man died from a laughing fit after seeing a gaudily dressed man from the East. He was credited with carving out several landforms while riding a tornado. One of his steeds was a mountain lion he wrestled to a standstill; another of his steeds was a horse fed on a diet of nitroglycerin and known as Widow-maker, who ended up killing his first wife, Slue-Foot Sue. He fell out of a covered wagon as an infant, and bears the name of the river he landed next to. Name this big man of the Wild West who was raised by coyotes and could talk to animals, the original cowboy.

A Purana named after this figure gives him authority over the Nine Pearls. For a time, his enemies thwarted his attacks by swallowing rocks, but Karambiya taught him a trick to force them to spit out the stones. On one occasion, he filled his mouth with the water of many rivers in order to put out a divine fire, then shrank himself in order to avoid some whirling blades. This occurred after Kadru imprisoned his mother Vinata, forcing this figure to steal amrita from the gods secure her release. Said to be large enough to block out the sun, he is the sworn enemy of the nagas. Name this king of birds, the mount of Vishnu.

In one story, the first man Mwuetsi takes this form when he is killed by his own descendants and thrown into the water. Deities in Dahomey culture associated with this object include Gleti, Ge and Mawu-Lisa. In the Dogon creation myth, Amma makes this object out of white earthenware bowls encircled in white copper, and in Ashanti myth, this object is represented by the sky god Nyame's left eye. In the Boshongo creation myth, this object comes into existence when Bumba vomits it out along with nine animals, stars and the Sun. The Egyptian god Thoth's ibis beak represented what celestial body's crescent form?

The name for these religious writings comes from the Sanskrit word for thread or warp. The writings consist of magical formulas, mostly in the context of discussions between Shiva and his wife Kali. These writings have spawned a religion, whose adherents practice a well-known form of Yoga. Name these writings, written in India in the 6th or 7th centuries.

The title character of this novel is an up and coming businessman, who uses his newfound wealth to move to a pretentious house in Boston, where he eventually disgraces himself by drinking too much at a dinner party given by the social elite. Although he is financially ruined by the end of the book, he has finally chosen to abandon his immoral money making schemes and has begun to recognize ethical standards. Name this 1885 novel, generally considered William Dean Howells' best work.

Born in 1950, he was nominated for a National Book Award for Union Dues, a novel which concerns a West Virginia miner who follows his runaway son to Boston at the height of the hippie movement. The next year, 1978, he turned to write for the screen, penning scripts for Piranha and The Howling, which financed his own first film, The Return of the Seacacus Recently he did an uncredited rewrite of Apollo 13, but his reputation lies with his independent work. FTP, who is this writer-director of Passion Fish and Lone Star?

The son of a schoolmaster, at age eleven he entered the Stadtkonvikt, where he studied for five years. He was a close friend of the operatic tenor Vogl, and after a walk with this friend, he wrote the Trout Quintet. Twice he stayed in Zseliz as tutor to Count Esterhazy's daughters and afterwards composed the Die Winterreise song cycle. FTP, name this composer of Alfonso and Estrella and Hark, Hark the Lark, who died of typhus in 1828, but who is more famous for his Great Symphony number 9 and his number eight, the Unfinished.

To improve his English, this writer translated James Baikie's Ancient Egypt into Arabic. A writer of screenplays, short stories, and novels, one collect ion of his short stories was called Dunya Allah, or God's World. Another wa s titled A Whisper of Madness. FTP, name this Egyptian winner of the 1988 Nobel Prize, whose major work was The Cairo Trilogy.

His cousin served as a judge at the trial of Charles I, and he himself published his first work, 'Heroic Stanzas,' upon the death of Cromwell. In the decade before his death in 1700, he translated all of Virgil, much of Ovid, and the first book of the Iliad. FTP, name the first poet laureate of England, author of ' MacFlecknoe' and 'Marriage a la Mode.'

This American playwright's major works include Golden Guts, Proud Flesh, and The Enchanted Hunters, none of which you will be able to find in any library. Equally unavailable is My Cue, the biographical memoir written about him by Vivian Darkbloom, although any good video store should carry the 1962 movie in which he was portrayed by Peter Sellers. FTP, name this non- existent writer and pedophile, who is assassinated by Humbert Humbert in the final chapter of Nabokov's Lolita.

Martin, the patriarch of this family, fathered two sets of children--one with a feeble-minded girl and one with his upper-class wife. Descendants on the respectable side included lawyers, doctors, and bankers, while the illegitimate union produced generation upon generation of alcoholics, criminals, mental defectives, and ugly persons. FTP, name this family, the subject of a bogus 1912 study written as propaganda for the eugenics movement, whose name is Greek for "good-bad."

He walks around dressed entirely in green, keeps a raven named Grip on his shoulder, and likes to yell and wave flags, which gets him into trouble when he is arrested and condemned to death for participating in the Gordon riots. FTP, name this hapless half-wit, the title character of what many consider to be Charles Dickens' worst novel.

After reading Darwin's _Voyage of the Beagle_, he set out on a similar tropical expedition of his own, but lost all of his work when the ship carrying his notes and specimens was destroyed by fire. Undeterred, he then made an eight-year trip to Borneo, where he composed an essay whose conclusions were almost identical to Darwin's still-unpublished _Origin of Species_. FTP, name this naturalist, who independently discovered Darwinian evolution.

Her first novel evolved from a letter to her grandfather. Her books involve the political realities and the role of women in Latin America, and are written in the magical realist tradition. She worked as a journalist in Chile until the 1973 assassination of her uncle. FTP, name this writer of Of Love and Shadows, Eva Luna, and The House of the Spirits.

The main character is a young Parisian boy, Antoine Doinel, who is increasingly defeated by the institutions of his life, including his selfish parents and his petty and cruel schoolteacher. Sent to a reform camp after stealing a typewriter, he escapes and runs to the sea. FTP, name this autobiographical major work of French New Wave Cinema, whose lead character would reappear in four later films by director Francois Truffaut.

His works include _The Challenge of World Poverty_ and _Crisis in the Population Question_, written with his wife. He shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Economics with Friedrich von Hayek for his "analysis of the interdependence of economic, social and institutional phenomena", an approach that was a significant factor in his best-known work, _An American Dilemma_. FTP, name the Swedish economist.

While working as a judge in London in the 1740s he founded the Bow Street Runners, a group that later was a model for the London police. He was in poor health late in life and his last book, The Journal of a Voyage to Lisbon, was written while he was looking for a better climate. His play The Historical Register for the Year 1736 inspired the Licensing Act of 1737, which ended his career as a playwright, but not before he wrote The Tragedy of Tragedies; or, The Life and Death of Tom Thumb the Great. For 10 points name this English author.

This collection includes "Elizabeth", "Emma and Eginhard", and "The Saga of King Olaf." It is modelled on Chaucer's Canterbury Tales and Boccaccio's Decameron. FTP, give the name of this American Collection of tales told by a group of New Englanders gathered around a fireplace whose most famous story is "Paul Revere's Ride."

Sandy's trip to St. Hubert in the West Indies hardly qualifies as a vacation, as his colleague Dr. Sondelius and his wife Leora both catch the plague which is running rampant there and die. To make matters worse, he's never certain whether the vaccine he made to combat the plague actually works. Name this title doctor from a 1925 Sinclair Lewis novel.

In a poem, Claude Shannon warns its owners to respect this, "keep it clean", and never lend it out, since "the most unkindest switch of all" renders it insoluble. Physicist Solomon Golomb likens quarks and antiquarks to clockwise and counterclockwise rotations of its corners, which in different configurations represent baryons or mesons. FTP name this maddening Hungarian invention, of which the shortest path to solving is known as God's algorithm.

This literary character lent her name to a genus of annelids and to a moon of Uranus. A work of non-fiction by Mary Pipher compared her fate to that of adolescent girls in the 1990's. A plant named for her in turn inspired the title of the Indigo Girls' last studio release. She was the subject of a famous 1852 painting by John Millais. FTP, name this Shakespearean tragic figure.

After a night of telling ghost stories, Douglas is persuaded to tell, on the following night, the story in a manuscript from an old gilt-edged album. In this manuscript, the narrator meets up with Mrs. Grose, who works in the house where the children she is to watch over, Miles and Flora, live. Name this ghost story, one of Henry James's most famous novels.

The title character and narrator loses his personal fortune when a merchant company goes bankrupt, then finds a new living under the villainous Squire Thornhill's patronage. After a series of tribulations, including being jailed, Primrose's fortune is eventually restored. These events summarize which book, the only novel ever written by Oliver Goldsmith?

According to the first verse of one translation of this work, the author "write[s] you this account, that all the brethren from among the heathen may know the miracles of our Lord Jesus Christ in His infancy, which He did after His birth in our country." FTP, this is the first line of the non-canonical gospel attributed to which apostle also called Didymos and doubter of Christ?

Based upon the novel D'Entre les Morts by Pierre Boileau and Thomas Narcejac, Vera Miles was groomed for several months to play the lead, but the movie's director said that she ‘became pregnant just before the part that was going to turn her into a star. After that I lost interest'. Part of the movie contrasts the frank, unfeminine Midge, played by Barbara Del Geddes, with the erotic, carnal Madeleine Elster, played by Kim Novak. For ten points name this Alfred Hitchcock movie which features Jimmy Stewart as John Ferguson, a retired police officer who has a fear of heights.

Although similar names had appeared in a 1561 Thomas Smith pamphlet, and tracts by John Oglander and David Hume, its name was coined by Sir Walter Scott in his novel Anne of Geierstein. Starting with a skirmish between the Percies and the Nevilles at Heworth Moor, the first main battle occurred when the Duke of Somerset's army was defeated at St. Albans by the forces of Warwick, Salisbury and York. Other battles of this war which lasted from 1455-85, include Northhampton, Tewkesbury and Bosworth Field. For ten points name this war which pitted the House of Lancaster against that of York.

Given money by John Home and Hugh Blair to conduct further searches through the highlands, he was unable to add any more works to the previous ones he had found, which included Temora, Fragments of Ancient Poetry Collected in the Highlands of Scotland, Translated from the Gallic or Erse Language, and Fingal. For ten points name this Scottish poet who claimed to have discovered works by a 3rd century poet named Ossian, but who actually wrote the works himself.

Although it may only be a legend, St. Jerome recorded, and Tennyson later repeated it in one of his poems, that this man was driven insane due to drinking a love potion that was given to him by his wife. During his periods of lucidity, he wrote his only work, a six-part poem, and committed suicide in 55 BC before he could complete it. The work, which was edited and published by Cicero, is a major source about the philosophy of Democritus and Epicurus and early scientific thought. For ten points name this Roman author of De rerum natura, or On the Nature of Things.

"I received your letter to-day by post, in regard to the ransom you ask for the return of my son. I think you are a little high in your demands, and I hereby make you a counter- proposition, which I am inclined to believe you will accept. You bring Johnny home and pay me $250 in cash, and I agree to take him off your hands."

Born in Cumberland in 1770, this poet's youth in the Lake District and Revolutionary France strongly influenced his works, known for their pastoral settings and linear conception of individual growth. The character "Lucy" from poems such as "Strange fits of passion I have known", "Three years she grew", and "A slumber did my spirit seal" has never been identified. FTP, name this poet, who left the massive poem "Prelude" unfinished at his death, and is known for other poems such as "The Two April Mornings", "Nutting", and "The Solitary Reaper".

"Where are Ella, Kate, Mag, Lizzie and Edith...One died in shameful child- brith, One of a thwarted love, One at the hands of a brute in a brothel...All are sleeping, sleeping on the hill." Thus is described the fate of a few of the over 200 subjects described in this collection of "auto-epitphs." FTP, identify this volume of verse depicting the residents in the cemetry of a Midwestern village, published in 1915 by Edgar Lee Masters.

Minor characters include a young and an old valet named, respectively, Vasha and Firs. Among this play's other characters are Charlotta Ivanovana, Yermolay Lopahin, and Pyotr Trofimov. The action of this play takes place on the estate of Madame Ranevsky. FTP, identify this play by Anton Chekhov.

This Victorian's poems are suffused with frustration and despair; however, he is better known for his novels, many of which exhibited a serial structure, and which emphasized the concept of naturalism. Most were set in his native Devon. FTP, name this author of the poems "A Broken Appointment" and the Darkling Thrush", and creator of such memorable characters as Eustachia Vye and Tess.

In 1884, this man went to Boston to teach, where he met William Dean Howells and began to write novels such as Jason Edwards and Rose Dutcher's Cooly. His Main-Travelled Roads is a collection of local color stories like "Under the Lion's Paw," but he is best known for an autobiographical work which won the 1922 Pulitzer Prize. FTP, who is this author of A Daughter of the Middle Border?

M.D. Hatch and C. R. Slack first worked out the biochemical pathway for this transformation. Typically seen in plants with Kranz anatomy like corn and sugarcane, it provides an advantage under conditions of high temperature and intense light, where plants are unable to use carbon dioxide effectively. FTP, what is this type of photosynthesis named for the compound which is broken down in the bundle-sheath cells?

This Old Testament book contains a dream of a statue with a head of gold, silver chest, bronze belly, iron legs, and feet of clay. In chapter 8 there is a vision of a lion, a bear, a leopard, and a many-horned terrifying beast. The next chapter contains a vision of a two-horned ram and a goat which destroys the ram. All these visions are interpreted by the same man who explains the meaning behind the words, "Mene, mene, tekel, parsin." FTP, name this book of the Bible or its main character who survives the lions' den.

Among his perversions was a fish-pond in which he would induce minnows to nibble at his genitals, and he owned a famous illustrated book of pornography by the author Elephantus. His restraint disappeared when his mother Livia died, and he allowed the Roman Empire to be run by his lieutenant Sejanus while he himself lived on the Isle of Capri. FTP, name this Emperor, the second of the Julio-Claudians.

This versatile author's works include a 1962 biography of the Marquis de Sade, as well as several works dealing with the issue of aging, such as A Very Easy Death and La Ceremonie des Adieux, which deals with the painful last years of the author's famous consort. An affair with Nelson Algren is believed to be the basis for the character of Lewis Brogan in The Mandarins. FTP, name this French author of Memoirs of a Dutiful Daughter and The Second Sex, perhaps best known for her lifelong association with Jean-Paul Sartre.

Its author's longest novel, it is set on the western front during World War I. The refusal of German and French armies to fight prompts Axis and Allied leaders to hold a conference at which they agree to continue the war. A man known as the Corporal, who was born in a stable on Christmas, is the leader of the insurrection, and is betrayed by the soldier Polchek and thrice denied by another soldier, Pierre. These events occur, FTP, in which religious allegory which won the 1955 Pulitzer Fiction Prize for William Faulkner?

The son was born in Australia, but traveled to the father's native England to pursue graduate studies. He later succeeded Ernest Rutherford at both Victoria University in Manchester and at the Cavendish at Cambridge, but is better known for work done as a student in collaboration with his father. FTP, give the surname of this father and son pair, who were awarded the 1915 Nobel prize in Physics for their work in X-ray crystallography.

Name the following English literary works. 15 points awarded on the first clue, 5 on the second. A. 15: In this novel, Higgs, the narrator, discovers a country, whose name identifies the book. The country's inhabitants worship the goddess Ypgrun. 5: This Samuel Butler work describes a society where the sick are imprisoned and criminals are hospitalized, and is an anagram for "nowhere".

Name the American author based on clues, 30-20-10 30: Since her death in 1947, none of her works has been filmed or televised, due to a stipulation in her will forbidding adaptation, which was inspired by the butchery of her novel "A Lost Lady" as a silent film. 20: She won the Pulitzer prize for fiction in 1923 for "One of Ours" 10: Although she was born in Virginia, her family settled in Red Cloud, Nebraska, which inspired her tales of the frontier.

This playwright's 1609 treatise "The New Art of Writing Plays" encouraged a new style, in which the classical unities were violated, and the denouement would not occur until the third of three acts. Some of his works include 'Fuenteovejuna", "El caballero de Olmedo", and "El mejor alcalde, el rey", and his "cloak-and- sword" plays dealing with love and intrigue were wildly popular, but less than one quarter of his prodigious output is extant. FTP, name this Spanish playwright whose 1800 plays makes him the most prolific playwright in history.

While majoring in English at Syracuse, she is said to have produced a manuscript of a novel every semester, and she has kept up her prolific writing pace. Noted for poetry, criticism, and short stories, she has also written novels in a multitude of genres, including the Gothic novels "Bellefleur" and "Mysteries of Winterthurn", and the mysteries "Lives of the Twins" and "Nemesis" under the pseudonym Rosamond Smith. FTP, name this American author of "Solstice", "A Garden of Earthly Delights", and "Them".

The narrator is rescued from Nukuheva and taken aboard the trader "Julia", where he befriends Dr. Long Ghost. After an imprisonment for mutiny on Tahiti, they explore the islands of Polynesia before the narrator signs aboard the whaler "Leviathan" \- a fitting plot for a novel whose title translates as "wanderer" in Marquesan. FTP, identify this Herman Melville novel, subtitled "A Narrative of Adventures in the South Seas", the sequel to "Typee".

Terrified of the new electric lights in the White House, he and his wife often left them on all night rather than touch the switch to turn them off. Despite the restrictions of the Pendleton Act, he completely ignored all civil-service qualifications and filled offices with party regulars. Ironically, though, he placed the young Teddy Roosevelt on the civil service commission. FTP--name this Republican who won office primarily with the support of the Grand Army of the Republic and defeated and was defeated by the same man in races for President.

Outside of Falstaff, its libretto is often considered the best work of its creator, Arrigo Boito. Boito's libretto followed its original source very closely except for Act II's Credo aria, which has no counterpart in the original and appears to have been Boito's invention. FTP--name this opera composed by Verdi and based on a Shakespearean play which tells the story of "The Lion of Venice."

The title character unknowingly violates the ground sacred to the Eumenides, and though initially welcomed by the local townspeople after he agrees to expiate for his unwitting act, the townspeople immediately demand that he and his daughter leave after they discover his true identity. Eventually, though, the king rescues his daughter from his cruel brother-in-law, and agrees to protect him until he dies. FTP--name this play, completed by its author while in his 90s, Sophocles' last though chronologically the middle play of his Theban trilogy.

He visited his twin sister St. Scholastica exactly once a year, and though he was not with her when she died, he had a vision of her in Paradise in a dream shortly thereafter. Known for his motto of "Ora et Labora"\--Prayer and Work--he originally was a hermit in a cave at Subiaco before founding his monastery at Monte Cassino. FTP--name this saint known for his "rule" which became the basis of monasticism in the West.

Though not Erma Bombeck, she also produced lighter semi- autobiographical works such as "Life Among the Savages" and "Raising Demons." Her posthumous collection of works, Just an Ordinary Day, includes "The Good Wife," a story of a newlywed wife kept prisoner by her husband, who suspects her of having an affair even though he writes the incriminating letters that he claims come from her lover. FTP--name this American writer more famous for a story appearing in 1948 in the New Yorker called "The Lottery."

An Old-Fashioned Girl is having one of her Moods again Under the Lilacs, but fortunately, after A Long Fatal Love Chase, she finds a Rose in Bloom and enjoys An Old-Fashioned Thanksgiving with her Eight Cousins. FTP--the preceding sentence features several works by what American author more famous for such works as Jo's Boys and Little Women?

Dorine the maid helps keep Mariane from becoming the wife of this "hypocrite", who tries to seduce Elmire right before her husband Orgon's very eyes and is only exposed just as he kicks Orgon's entire family out of their own house. Name this title character of a comedy by Moliere.

Several months before he died in 1983, he was given Spain's highest civilian award, the Grand Cross of Isabel, for work which had led to his exile from his homeland for almost 40 years. His autobiography, My Last Sigh, was published posthumously. Some of this director's work includes That Obscure Object of Desire and the Oscar winner The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie. FTP, name the director who collaborated with Dali on the film, An Andalusian Dog?

In this poem, the narrator revisits his childhood home where he and Amy, his cousin, had fallen in love. Amy was, however, a shallow young woman who went with her parents' wishes that she marry a wealthy young man. At the beginning, he protests this world, but later learns to accept the inevitability of change. FTP, identify the poem by naming the home visited again by Tennyson some "Sixty Years After".

As a young man, this author dropped out of Kazan University without recieving his medical degree. Later, he became an army officer and participated in the seige of Sevastopol during the Crimean War. In 1876, he had a religious awakening and freed the serfs on his land. FTP, identify this author known for The Kreutzer Sonata.

Born in 1873 to a wealthy Richmond family, she lived the life of a Southern belle but rebelled against this lifestyle in her works. While an apprentice to a local writer, she wrote The Voice of the People, a social history of her home state from 1850 on. She first gained serious literary attention with 1924's Barren Ground which was followed by The Sheltered Life, both socio- histories of Virginia as seen through the eyes of a woman. FTP, name this American novelist, best known for the Pulitzer Prize winning In This Our Life and for The Romantic Comedians.

An unsuccessful candidate for Parliament in 1868, he is the author of such psychological novels as Kept in the Dark and Sir Harry Hotspur of Humblethwaite. 1865's Can You Forgive Her intoduced the future Duke of Omnium, Plantagenet Palliser, the subject of a series of political novels. FTP, name this writer, a sometime postal clerk best known for The Warden, The Small House at Allington and several other novels about the town of Barsetshire.

This novel takes as its subject three generations of a theatrical family; the youngest, Kim Hawks, grows up to become a Broadway star. Her mother Magnolia was an actress who had Kim by the actor Gaylord Ravenal; Magnolia is the daughter of Captain Andy Hawks, who runs the novel's title object on the Mississippi river. FTP, name this 1926 Edna Ferber novel made, in the year after its publication, into a musical with music by Jerome Kern and libretto by Oscar Hammerstein.

The main character of this work is a jazz-playing ex-student from a "white tile" university who derisively chooses to work in a street market; the woman is the daughter of a colonel. As the play opens, Alison is ironing the clothes of her husband and their lodger, Cliff; when Alison reveals herself to be pregnant, her husband leaves her and goes to live with Helena, a childhood friend. Later, Jimmy and his wife reunite after the pregnancy fails. FTP, name this 1957 play about the Porters, written by John Osborne.

"We must discard with the old ways and submit to technology!.. We must be like the automobile, beautiful with its power and speed!.. We must forcefully overthrow the shackles of culture and the staleness of the past in order to advance!" Such are excerpts from an article published in 1909 by Le Figaro, which was written as a manifesto for a new artistic movement. FTP, give the name of this movement, subscribed to by such artists as Gino Severini, Carlo Carra, and Umberto Boccioni, and founded by Filipino Marinetti.

Industrialist Gerald Crich falls in love with Gudrun Brangwen, but their relationship is troubled by possessiveness. Gudrun's sister Ursula, on the other hand, enjoys a more enlightened marriage to authorial mouthpiece Rupert Birkin, whose offers of friendship are spurned by Crich. The characters in this novel are probably based on the author's friends John Middleton Murry and Katherine Mansfield, the author himself, and his wife Frieda. FTP, name this 1920 sequel to "The Rainbow" by D.H. Lawrence.

His 1906 story collection, "City of the Yellow Devil", expressed a hostility toward the United States, and especially New York, which was probably fueled by the negative reaction to the presence of his mistress on a tour of the United States. His three-part autobiography relates his harsh upbringing at the hands of his grandfather, and his subsequent life as a tramp throughout czarist Russia. He is also remembered as a novelist, literary critic, and the author of plays such as "The Lower Depths." FTP, name this bitter man, whose real name was Aleksei Peshkov.

"Hope," "Blood," and the name of the title character are the three answers that Calaf must supply in order to keep his head and win the title lady's hand in marriage. "Love" is in turn the answer she gives to his counter challenge, after Liu shows the power of her own love, choosing to stab herself rather than reveal Calaf's name. This is the grand finale of, FTP, what Puccini opera, in which the heralds proclaim "Nessun Dorma""until the answer to the final riddle is found, no one shall sleep in Peking?

He began working as an attorney in Boston in 1920, but left three years later for France to pursue his avocation. Influenced while in France by Pound and Eliot, he published "The Happy Marriage", "The Pot of Earth", and "Streets in the Moon". After returning the the United States, he wrote a verse play based on Genesis called "Nobodaddy", and the collection "New Found Land", which included "You, Andrew Marvell". In 1939 he was appointed Librarian of Congress, and was an assistant secretary of state during World War II. FTP, name this poet awarded a Pulitzer Prize for his 1932 poem "Conquistador", the author of "Ars Poetica".

His 1981 book "From Bauhaus to Our House" argued that contemporary American architecture fails to reflect its society, and "In Our Time" is a collection of his drawings. Author of "The Pump House Gang", "The Purple Decades", and "Mauve Gloves & Madmen, Clutter & Vine", in which he explored American pop culture, he has coined such phrases as "radical chic" and "the me decade". FTP, name this "new journalist" who wrote "The Kandy-Kolored Tangerine- Flake Streamline Baby", "The Right Stuff", and "The Electric Kool- Aid Acid Test".

Walker Percy was teaching at Loyola in 1976 when a woman presented him a badly smeared, scarcely readable manuscript of a novel written during the early 60's by her son. The novel's characters include Myrna Minkoff, a woman transported from her native Bronx to New Orleans, the eccentric Mrs. Reilly, and her son Ignatius who, lying in his flannel shirt in a back bedroom on Constantinople Street, is filling dozens of Big Chief tablets with invective against the modern age. FTP identify this perverse Pulitzer Prize winning comedy by John Kennedy Toole.

Finally, the name of Don Juan's servant has changed several times. Tirso calls him Catalinon, Moliere uses Sganarelle, and there are dozens of other.
